# Initialisation
First access required modules.
```{julia}
using Compose, Colors, Measures
import EpidemicsCFTP
epi = EpidemicsCFTP ;
```

A laconic description of the `julia` package `Compose.jl` 
(the graphics package used for these figures)
is provided at 
<https://giovineitalia.github.io/Compose.jl/latest/>.

Basic simulation parameters are the `population` size 
and the `duration` (assumes epidemic simulation commences at time `0`).
Note that (trivial) labelling issues arise if `population > MAXPOP=20`.
```{julia}
const population = 5 ;
const duration   = 2 ;

const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if population > MAXPOP
  error("`population` exceeds `$(MAXPOP)`: modify code indexing time-lines!")
end ;
```

We now set up and establish graphics size, coordinates, and drawing region.
```{julia}
set_default_graphic_size(6inch, 4inch) ;

coordinates = UnitBox(0, population, duration, -population, 
                      leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, 
                      bottompad=0.5inch, toppad=0.5inch) ;
region      = (context(), rectangle(), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.3)) ;
```


# Basic image template elements
First construct the time axis, with tick marks at integer times.
Note, here and following,  careful use of graphics area units (`cx`, `cy`) 
```{julia}
tic       = -0.2cy
step      = 10^floor(Int, log10(duration))
tic_loc1  = [(((x)cx,0cy), ((x)cx, tic))    for x in 0:1.0step:duration]
tic_loc2  = [(((x)cx,0cy), ((x)cx, tic))    for x in 0:0.5step:duration]
tic_loc3  = [(((x)cx,0cy), ((x)cx, 0.5tic)) for x in 0:0.1step:duration]

label_height = 0cy + 0.25inch
labellocs    = [(x)cx for x in 0:duration]

time_axis = (context(),
   line([(0cx, 0cy), ((duration)cx, 0cy)]), stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.5mm),
   (context(), line(tic_loc1), stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.2mm)),
   (context(), line(tic_loc2), stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.1mm)),
   (context(), line(tic_loc3), stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.1mm)),
   (context(), text(labellocs, [label_height], ["$i" for i in 0:duration], 
      [hcenter], [vcenter]), stroke("grey"), fontsize(7pt)) ) ;
```


Now build the time-lines, labelled by circled integers.
The definition of `circlabels` below needs to be changed if `population > MAXPOP=20`,
as unicode then runs out of circled integers!
```{julia}
circlabels   = [string(Char(0x00002460+i-1)) for i in 1:population]

lines        = (context(), 
  line([[(0cx, (k)cy), ((duration)cx, (k)cy)] for k in 1:population]), 
      stroke("black"), linewidth(0.5mm), 
  (context(),
  text([0cx-0.25inch], [(k)cy for k in 1:population], circlabels,
      [hleft], [vcenter]), stroke("black"), fontsize(10pt)) ) ;
```

Finally we build a tree describing the construction of scaffolding.
```{julia}
scaffolding = (context(), region, (context(), time_axis, lines) ) ;
```

# Drawing the underlying scaffolding
@fig-scaffolding illustrates the underlying scaffolding for (almost) all our diagrams:
```{julia}
#| label: fig-scaffolding
#| fig-cap: "Scaffolding"
compose(context(units=coordinates), scaffolding)
```

# An innovation for an unconditioned \(SIR\) epidemic
We introduce some content by considering potential incidents underlying
an unconditional epidemic.
```{julia}
A = epi.AbstractInfection ; 
I = epi.Infection ; P = epi.PInfection ; R = epi.Removal ; C = epi.CRemoval

env0 = epi.Innovation(5, 
  A[
    I(0.2,2,5), I(0.4,1,2), P(0.5,1,2), I(0.6,2,4), I(0.85,3,4), I(0.9,2,3),
    I(1.0,1,2), I(1.05,4,5), I(1.11,1,4), I(1.2,2,4), I(1.6,3,5), I(1.5,3,4)
    ], 
  R[R(0.3,5), R(0.42,3), R(0.95,5), R(1.4,2)],
  C[C(1.3,2), C(0.8,1), C(1.7,4), C(1.8,4), C(1.92,5)]
) ;
```

We now add a graphical depiction of the potential incidents supplied by the innovation.
Elements are plotted in reverse-order: for example, the first in sequence overlays 
all subsequent elements. @fig-potential illustrates the required plot.

```{julia}
radius = 0.2cy
bit    = -0.02h
elements = (context(), # Labels (Infections) 
  (context(),
    text([(inc.t)cx for inc in env0.infections],
         [(inc.infector)cy for inc in env0.infections], 
         [string(inc) for inc in env0.infections],
         [hcenter], [vcenter]), fontsize(5pt), font("Helvetica"), ),                    
    
  (context(),          # Labels (Removals)
    text([(inc.t)cx for inc in env0.removals],
         [(inc.target)cy for inc in env0.removals], 
         [string(inc) for inc in env0.removals],
         [hcenter], [vcenter]), fontsize(5pt), font("Helvetica"), ),                    

  (context(),          # Labels (Conditional Removals)
    text([(inc.t)cx for inc in env0.cremovals],
         [(inc.target)cy for inc in env0.cremovals], 
         [string(inc) for inc in env0.cremovals],
         [hcenter], [vcenter]), fontsize(5pt), font("Helvetica"), ),                    

  (context(),          # Infection contacts
    line([[((inc.t)cx, (inc.infector)cy+radius), ((inc.t)cx, (inc.infectee)cy)]
           for inc in env0.infections]),
    line([[((inc.t)cx - 0.3bit, (inc.infectee)cy-bit), 
           ((inc.t)cx,          (inc.infectee)cy), 
           ((inc.t)cx + 0.3bit, (inc.infectee)cy-bit)]
           for inc in env0.infections]), stroke("orange")),
  
  (context(),          # Perpetuated infections
    circle([(inc.t)cx for inc in env0.infections if isa(inc, P)], 
           [(inc.infector)cy for inc in env0.infections if isa(inc, P)],
           [radius]), fill("white"), stroke("darkgreen")),                  

  (context(),          # Infections
    circle([(inc.t)cx for inc in env0.infections if isa(inc, I)], 
           [(inc.infector)cy for inc in env0.infections if isa(inc, I)],
           [radius]), fill("white"), stroke("orange")),                      

  (context(),          # Removals
    circle([(inc.t)cx for inc in env0.removals], 
           [(inc.target)cy for inc in env0.removals],
           [radius]), fill("white"), stroke("blue")),                        

  (context(),          # Conditional Removals
    circle([(inc.t)cx for inc in env0.cremovals], 
           [(inc.target)cy for inc in env0.cremovals],
           [radius]), fill("white"), stroke("purple")),                     
);
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-potential
#| fig-cap: "Potential incidents, including both removals and infections:                                 \
#|           Potential removals (R for _removal_) are indicated by disks with blue outlines,              \
#|           conditional removals (C for _conditioned_) are indicated by disks with purple outlines,      \
#|           potential infections (I for _infected_) are indicated by disks with orange outlines,         \
#|           perpetuated infections (P for _perpetuated_) are indicated by disks with dark green outlines.\
#|           Orange arrows indicate connections of potential infector time-lines                          \
#|           to corresponding potential infectee time-lines.                                              \
#|           Each disk is annotated by the summary description of the corresponding incident."

compose(context(units=coordinates), elements, scaffolding)
```

# Evolving the epidemic in process time
Next we must plot the course of epidemics arising from the time-sequence `chron` of potential incidents
supplied by the innovation. The time sequence is derived from the innovation
by the `chronology` function, and we need to compute the trajectory,
and history of realized incidents, corresponding to a specific initial state at time \(0.0\),
given by an `SIR` structure. Application of `evolution_recurse!`, working destructively on the input lists, delivers the \(SIR\) trajectory `traj`, and lists realized incidents in `active`.

::: {.callout-caution}
Re-work `evolution_recurse!` to be non-destructive of its arguments!
:::

First of all, we use the `traj` argument to produce a plot against time of the numbers of
susceptibles, infectives and removed individuals. We begin by generating a dataframe
recording the trajectories as the knots of piecewise constant functions.
```{julia}
t1     = 2.0                       # Final time
states = [epi.SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0)]   # Initial state list (will be overwritten)
chron  = epi.chronology(env0)      # Empty list (will be overwritted)
traj, active = epi.evolution_recurse!(states, epi.AbstractIncident[], t1, chron)

using DataFrames
t = [state.t for state in traj]
push!(t, t1)
t = repeat(t, inner=2)[2:(end-1)]

s = repeat([state.s for state in traj], inner=2)
i = repeat([state.i for state in traj], inner=2)
r = repeat([state.r for state in traj], inner=2)
df = DataFrame(t=t, Susceptibles=s, Infectives=i, Removals=r)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-trajectories
#| fig-cap: Trajectories in time of susceptibles, infections and removals.   

import Gadfly
Gadfly.plot(df, x=:t, y=Gadfly.Col.value(:Susceptibles, :Infectives, :Removals), 
  color=Gadfly.Col.index(:Susceptibles, :Infectives, :Removals), 
  Gadfly.Geom.line)
```
